profile.headline: Software Developer II | Amazon Ads (Rufus AI, Agentic Shopping)
profile.summary:
As a Software Developer II at Amazon, I participate in the development of multiple enterprise-level microservices that drive over 1 million monthly active users to Alexa. I led, designed, and implemented a feature that allows users to create routines using voice, which has reached more than 100,000 MAU since its launch. I also work with different teams and dive deep into our natural language processing stack to create custom targeting logic for groups.

My passion for software development and innovation stems from my education and personal ventures. I graduated from Emory University with a Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science, where I was an executive board member of the Tech Division at Emory Entrepreneurship & Venture Management and HackATL. I won the EEVM Internal Pitch Competition with a concept of a VR animation suite that makes 3D models much more intuitive to manipulate. I recruited talent and created a demo using Unity, and delegated tasks to my team in a manner that encourages both progress and individuality. I am skilled in Ultimaker Cura, C#, Node.js, and 3D modeling, and I am always eager to learn new technologies and tools.

positions.title: Software Developer II - Amazon Ads (Rufus AI, Now Alexa Plus)
positions.description:
* Built an MCP-powered autonomous development agent that writes, tests, and validates code across three
backend services — enabling fully asynchronous task completion with self-verifying feedback loops, reducing
end-to-end development time by 70%+
* Built an automated pipeline to optimize wording of AI-generated answer pills, increasing click-through rate by
50%
* Led backend design, implementation, and launch of Rufus Pills (AI-generated, interactive chatbot ads), driving
$1.4M+ MRR in new monetization streams
* Collaborated with data scientists and ML engineers to scale LLM inference pipelines and agent systems serving
100M+ users
* Designed and built an LLM-powered sales agent with RAG-based retrieval, brand-specific prompt routing, and
multi-step, stateful orchestration workflows with tool-use capabilities
